incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: routing-tier flap detected (dynamic-tier controller) — observed repeated tier threshold oscillation across us-east-1 and eu-west-2 starting 2026-11-02T14:45Z. Auto-fallback engaged twice. Severity: P1.

matt_oncall: acked. I'm on it. paging ana_sre and jin_eng. tagging infra owners.

ana_sre: (typo) ana_sre here, joining. first pass: metrics look like request spikes -> tier demote -> fallback to cheaper model -> latency spikes -> upstream retries -> spillover.

jin_eng: grabbing logs. can someone share the exact dynamic-tier config that rolled out? I see a config bump around 14:40.

matt_oncall: @sara_ops pushed dynamic-tier v0.9.3 at 14:38 UTC (canary -> global).

sara_ops: yep that was me, small operator tweak to the scale-in threshold to be more aggressive. didn't expect oscillation. rolling it back if we confirm.

nilesh_ml: note: fallback-model selection changed too (prefer-compat turned on) in the same deploy window — might be correlated.

matt_oncall: timeline quick dump:
- 14:38 deploy: dynamic-tier v0.9.3 (scale-in threshold -10%) + fallback compat toggle
- 14:45 first spike detected us-east-1 tier B
- 14:47 automatic demote -> traffic routed to fallback-model-q8 (higher latency)
- 14:50 retries increase, 5xx up 0.3% region-wide
- 14:54 eu-west-2 begins receiving spillover from us-east-1 (tier capacity exceeded)
- 15:02 second oscillation observed, auto-fallback again

jin_eng: log snippet from router-6 (us-east-1):
```
[2026-11-02T14:45:12Z] ROUTER INFO req=0x8a3f tier=B load=0.92 threshold=0.8 action=demote -> fallback-model-q8
[2026-11-02T14:45:13Z] KV_CACHE WARN miss_rate=0.34
[2026-11-02T14:45:14Z] PROXY ERR upstream=encoder-3 timeout=120ms retries=1
```

ana_sre: interesting: demote happened even though burst buffer still had slots. looks like the controller computed available capacity incorrectly after the threshold change.

nilesh_ml: fallback-model-q8 is quantized and cheaper but has higher token-latency under concurrency; that explains the latency bump for user-facing routes.

sam_product: customer impact: two enterprise customers in us-east saw sustained p50 increase from 120ms -> 780ms between 14:50-15:10. one reported UI lag. no data exfil or corrupted responses.

matt_oncall: mitigation steps taken so far:
- 15:06 rolled back dynamic-tier config to previous values (sara_ops)
- 15:10 forced routing to prefer primary model variant for high-tier customers (manual override)
- 15:12 increased burst capacity temporarily in us-east-1 (scale-up)

jin_eng: after rollback, we see tier stabilization. latency trending down in graphs. still see a couple of stragglers.

ana_sre: hypothesis list (working):
1) threshold change in v0.9.3 mis-calculates effective capacity under short bursts -> premature demotion.
2) fallback-model selection change (prefer-compat) made router pick slower quantized models more often -> amplified latency.
3) routing policy tie-breaker favors region spillover instead of queuing, causing eu-west-2 load bump.

matt_oncall: evidence mapping:
- hypothesis 1 supported by controller logs: incorrect available_slots computation at 14:45. (see controller-logs dump).
- hypothesis 2 supported by audit of fallback decision table — compat flag flipped at 14:37.
- hypothesis 3 weaker, need routing traces to confirm tiebreaker behavior.

nilesh_ml: will pull model selection traces and sample responses for quality/latency.

jin_eng: I've uploaded a focused log bundle to the incident folder: https://redwood.internal/ops/incidents/1796054321/logs (contains router, controller, kvcache, model-proxy traces).

sam_product: customer comms: we should notify the two affected customers with a short note: impact details + mitigation steps + ETA for RCA. I'll draft. :thumbsup:

matt_oncall: can someone own a short blameless summary for the next shift? I'll hand off in 30m.

ana_sre: I'll prepare a runnable repro (stress test) for the dynamic-tier controller in staging. will link results.

sara_ops: I will revert the fallback-compat toggle in the config registry and lock it behind a kill-switch. also adding a canary gate.

matt_oncall: handoff to @ana_sre for on-call in 30m. Key artifacts to keep in mind: log bundle link, timeline above, rollback action performed, affected customer list in customer-inbox.

ana_sre: taking over. summary for next-oncall: dynamic-tier v0.9.3 induced premature demotes due to undercounted available_slots under burst; fallback selection then routed many requests to quantized fallback-model-q8; the combination caused latency and spillover into eu-west-2. mitigations: rollback v0.9.3, forced primary routing for high-tier customers, temporary burst scale-up.

matt_oncall: thanks team. I'll open the RCA doc and assign owners for each hypothesis. please add any additional logs/evidence to the doc.

incident-bot: Incident status changed -> Mitigated at 2026-11-02T15:12Z. Incident severity downgraded to P2. Postmortem requested: https://redwood.internal/ops/postmortems/1796054321

ana_sre: postmortem checklist started. owners: controller fix (jin_eng), fallback policy audit (nilesh_ml), deploy gating improvements (sara_ops), customer comms (sam_product). assigning now.

matt_oncall: closing chat for active mitigation. any followups, ping here and I'll re-open. :white_check_mark:
